item.description:

item.title: Black on Campus: A film screening & panel discussion — Tue Nov 10, 3:30 PM — (3rd flr York Lanes
item.description: Black on Campus: A film screening & panel discussion ⏰ Tuesday 10th, November, 3:30pm – 6pm 📍 Hybrid: online | and @ the Harriet Tubman Institute, 314 York Lanes, YorkU 🔗 Register here. (limited in-person space) 🍕 Food and refreshments will be served. 😷 Masking is encouraged, and available for free at the door. Join us for a short film screening of “Black on Campus” followed by a panel discussion about anti-black racism on university campuses. The recent death of Cambridge University professor Jason Arday has brought renewed attention to the experience of blackness in academia. Our panelists will elaborate on thinking about anti-black racism not just as an event, but a structure that shapes the lives of black students, staff, and faculty. Also learn about the campaign supporting Dr Aimé Avolonto and Lydia Dosu’s struggle against anti-black racism at York University. item.title: A Soirée for Curious Minds: Has Canada Fixed Its Immigration and Asylum Policy? — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Is Canada’s immigration system keeping pace with a rapidly changing world? Join Professor Michael Barutciski of Glendon College, York University, for a timely and thought-provoking evening exploring Canada’s evolving immigration and asylum policies. From caps on temporary residents to stricter border controls, discover what recent policy changes mean for Canada’s future and whether they address the deeper challenges facing the system. A lawyer and recognized specialist in Canadian and international public affairs, Professor Barutciski brings extensive experience advising governments and international organizations. Part of A Soirée for Curious Minds, presented by Glendon College in partnership with Rosedale United Church, the evening promises an engaging blend of expert insight, live piano music and stimulating conversation in an intimate, welcoming setting.
Source: York University

item.title: CAIS Talks with Azadeh Tabiban — Thu Nov 12, 11:00 AM — 519 Kaneff Tower
item.description:
The Centre for Artificial Intelligence & Society presents: CAIS Talks with Azadeh Tabiban
Date: Thursday, November 12, 2026 Time: 11:00am-12:30pm EST Location: Kaneff Tower 519
On the Robustness of Learning-based Intrusion Detectors
Abstract: Provenance-based intrusion detection systems (PIDSes) are a promising approach for detecting sophisticated attacks. Learning-based PIDSes learn from the captured causal relationships between events to identify malicious system entities based on their context. However, can these detectors remain effective when attackers surround malicious entities with carefully chosen benign-looking events? In this talk, I will present Contorter, an evasion framework that leverages node-level PIDS embeddings to guide the generation of effective benign-looking events. item.title: Seminar Series 2026 – 2027 – Adrien Gandolfo (Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 and a researcher at IRCELYON in France) — Thu Nov 12, 1:30 PM — 140 Campus Walk
item.description: Title: Sources and sinks of NO₂ in forested environments: the role of multiphase chemistry Abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is at the crossroads of tropospheric oxidation chemistry. Its photolysis drives ozone (O₃) production, and its heterogeneous conversion yields nitrous acid (HONO), a major primary source of OH radicals. In forested environments, NOx levels are low and surface areas are large. Multiphase processes on soils, leaves and aerosols can therefore determine whether these surfaces act as a sink or a source of NO₂. Yet these processes remain poorly constrained in atmospheric models. In this talk, I will first address the sink side, presenting NO₂ uptake at the ground from soil flux measurements. On the source side, I will focus on nitrate photolysis in high-ionic-strength media as a renoxification pathway. Finally, I will assess the impact of these processes on HONO and O₃ in a modelled forested area. Bio: Adrien Gandolfo is an Assistant Professor at Lyon 1 University, Fran

item.title: Tubman Talks Roundtable Discussion: Threading Antiblackness in the SWANA region — Thu Nov 12, 2:00 PM — (3rd flr York Lanes
item.description: Date: Thursday, November 12, 2026 Time: 2:00-3:30pm EST Location: Tubman Resource Room (314 York Lanes) (Hybrid) 4700 Keele Street Toronto, ON | M3J 1P3 In-Person Registration: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/wukKRRswxp Zoom Registration: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/y3dPgh8eSyaKkX8eOnAp6g Title: Threading Antiblackness in the SWANA region Abstract: This talk examines antiblackness as a constitutive and enduring structure across the afterlives of slavery in the SWANA (Southwest Asia and North Africa) region. Bringing together case studies from different parts of the region (Libya, Tunisia, and Yemen), we foreground how historical regimes of enslavement—particularly the trans-Saharan and Indian Ocean slave trades—continue to shape contemporary racial hierarchies, policies, and everyday experiences of Blackness. Dan Yashinsky is a storyteller and writer based in Toronto.
